intro.author: Not named in the book; Jewish and Christian tradition credits Jeremiah, though many scholars think another eyewitness poet (or poets) wrote it
intro.written: Soon after Jerusalem fell to Babylon in 586 BC
intro.audience: The survivors of Judah, both those left in the ruined land and those taken into exile
intro.setting: Nebuchadnezzar's Babylonian army besieged Jerusalem for about eighteen months, starved the city, then burned the temple, tore down the walls and carried many people away. Lamentations is five poems of grief written in the ashes of that disaster.
intro.purpose: To give honest words to unbearable loss, to confess the sin that led to judgment, and to keep praying to God when every visible sign of his favor was gone.
intro.bigIdea: Even in the ruins, grief can be brought to God, and his mercies are not finished.

outline.title: Jerusalem the widow, with no one to comfort her
The Lord's anger against his own city

The people's prayer: remember us, restore us
